title: Locating Places on the Earth — Chapter Summary
intro: To find any place on Earth precisely, we use a system of imaginary lines: latitudes (parallels) running east-west, and longitudes (meridians) running north-south. Together they form the geographic grid. This chapter introduces the equator and Prime Meridian, the named parallels (Tropics, Polar Circles, Poles), heat zones, and how to read coordinates.

sections.heading: Earth's Shape and Globes/Maps
bullets: Earth is an OBLATE SPHEROID — a slightly flattened sphere.
Spinning axis ends at the NORTH POLE and the SOUTH POLE.
Earth rotates once in 24 hours, giving day and night.
GLOBE = round model; most accurate for shape/size; hard to carry.
MAP = flat drawing; easy to carry, shows detail; distorts somewhat.

sections.heading: Latitudes (Parallels)
bullets: East-west lines parallel to the equator.
Equator = 0°; poles = 90° (N or S).
Tropic of Cancer = 23½° N; Tropic of Capricorn = 23½° S.
Arctic Circle = 66½° N; Antarctic Circle = 66½° S.
Heat zones — Torrid (between tropics), Temperate (tropics to polar circles), Frigid (inside polar circles).

sections.heading: Longitudes (Meridians)
bullets: North-south lines from pole to pole; all the same length.
Prime Meridian = 0° (passes through Greenwich, England).
Measured 0° to 180° east AND 0° to 180° west of Prime Meridian.
180° meridian = INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE — calendar date changes when crossing.
Eastern hemisphere = east of Prime Meridian; Western = west of it.

sections.heading: The Geographic Grid — Reading Coordinates
bullets: Every place has a unique (latitude, longitude) pair.
Format: latitude FIRST, then longitude. N/S for lat, E/W for long.
New Delhi ≈ (28.6° N, 77.2° E).
To FIND a place: trace the parallel + meridian; their intersection IS the place.

sections.heading: Time Zones and Standard Time
bullets: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours = 15° per hour.
Each 15° of longitude → 1 hour of time difference.
1° of longitude = 4 minutes.
India uses INDIAN STANDARD TIME (IST), set to 82.5° E (passing through Mirzapur).
When Greenwich is 12 noon, India is 5:30 pm.
Large countries with multiple time zones (USA, Russia) split into several. India uses just one for simplicity.

key_takeaways: Earth is a slightly flattened sphere; spinning axis ends at the two poles.
Equator (0° latitude) and Prime Meridian (0° longitude) are the master reference lines.
Latitudes run east-west; longitudes run north-south.
Named parallels: equator, Tropic of Cancer (23½° N), Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S), Arctic Circle (66½° N), Antarctic Circle (66½° S).
Three heat zones: Torrid, Temperate, Frigid.
Coordinates of a place are written (latitude, longitude); always read latitude first.
Earth turns 15° per hour; IST is at 82.5° E.

glossary.definition: A slightly flattened sphere; the actual shape of the Earth.
The two endpoints of the Earth's spinning axis — North Pole and South Pole.
A round 3D model of the Earth.
A flat drawing of the Earth (or part of it).
An imaginary east-west line on the Earth, parallel to the equator. Measured in degrees N or S of the equator.
The 0° parallel; divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.
The parallel at 23½° N latitude. Passes through India.
The parallels at 66½° N and 66½° S respectively; boundaries of the Frigid Zones.
The Torrid (between tropics), Temperate (tropics to polar circles), and Frigid (inside polar circles) zones based on latitude.
An imaginary north-south line from pole to pole.
The 0° meridian, passing through Greenwich, England.
The 180° meridian; calendar date changes when crossed.
A pair (latitude, longitude) that uniquely identifies a place on Earth.
A region using the same standard time; based on a chosen meridian (e.g. India's IST = 82.5° E).
